chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Mawsawi narrated to me from Ubayd Allah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd Al-Shahham, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, Allah will forgive him his past and future sins. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Arafah, Allah will record for him the reward of one thousand accepted Hajj and one thousand purified 'Umrah. And whoever visits him on the Day of 'Ashura, it is as if he has visited Allah above [in] His Throne.

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting Imam Al-Husayn on the fifteenth of Sha'ban and the Day of 'Ashura?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s seminal work *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the theological significance of Ziyarat as a means of attaining divine proximity and expiation. The specific rewards highlight the unique status of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) in Shia piety, linking his martyrdom to cosmic events like the Night of Decree and the Day of Standing, thereby elevating the physical act of visitation to a spiritual encounter with the Divine Presence.
